title: BIZRA Degraded Experience Constitution v1.0
description: Defines what a weaker node may do, what it must never fake, what it must persist, and when it must refuse instead of pretending. This document protects equal citizenship across unequal hardware.

principles.principle_1: Honest degradation is always better than silent failure or fake quality.
principles.principle_2: A phone running 0.5B model is a full citizen with degraded execution, not a second-class citizen.
principles.principle_3: The URP exists to lift weaker nodes to the constitutional floor, not to replace them.
principles.principle_4: Every degradation must be declared in the receipt. Hidden degradation is a constitutional violation.
principles.principle_5: A node that cannot meet the minimum Ihsan floor even with URP help must refuse, not pretend.

tier_0_full.description: Node meets all requirements locally. No degradation.
tier_0_full.example: NODE0 with 30B model, full memory, full retrieval

tier_1_light_degradation.description: Node handles most work locally but some optional features are skipped.
tier_1_light_degradation.example: Laptop with 7B model, no vision capability

tier_2_significant_degradation.description: Node can generate a response but quality is below target. URP enriches.

tier_3_urp_assisted.description: Node cannot produce acceptable output alone. URP provides primary compute.
tier_3_urp_assisted.example: Very weak device, no local model, or all models below 0.5B
tier_3_urp_assisted.urp_involvement: URP runs inference on behalf of node. Local PAT still authors the receipt.

tier_4_refused.description: Node cannot contribute to this mission even with URP help. Mission is refused honestly.
tier_4_refused.example: Mission requires vision but no vision model exists anywhere in the path
tier_4_refused.outcome: Mission fails with FailureCode::CapabilityNotAvailable. Receipt emitted.
tier_4_refused.urp_involvement: None — refusal is the constitutionally correct outcome

must_never_fake.description: Things a degraded node must NEVER pretend to have done.
rules: Never claim retrieval happened if it was skipped
Never claim a model was used that was not actually used
Never claim Ihsan score was computed if scoring was skipped
Never claim memory was extracted if extraction failed
Never claim Guardian approved if Guardian was not consulted
Never emit a receipt without the actual degradation flags
Never claim local execution if URP handled inference
Never forge the resource snapshot — it must reflect actual hardware at submission time

must_always_persist.description: Things that must be persisted even in the most degraded path.
rules: The mission receipt (even if degraded or failed)
The degradation reasons array (complete, not partial)
The resource snapshot at submission time
The model actually used (or 'none' if URP delegated)
The mission state history (all transitions, with timestamps)

must_always_emit_receipt.description: Receipt emission is constitutional. These receipts are always required.
conditions: On degraded completion (degraded state, with all degradation reasons)
On failure (failed state, with failure code)
On timeout (timed_out state, with partial results if any)
On URP rejection (rejected by SAT, with reason)
On local refusal (capability not available, with honest declaration)
must_always_emit_receipt.invariant: There is no code path that terminates a mission without emitting a receipt.

when_to_refuse.description: A node must refuse a mission (not attempt it) when:
conditions: No model available for required capability, and URP cannot assist
Ihsan score is below degradation floor (0.85) and cannot be recovered
Resource snapshot shows insufficient RAM/VRAM to even load a fallback model
Guardian detects constitutional violation in the mission request itself
Node is in Stopped or Degraded state with no recovery path
when_to_refuse.invariant: Honest refusal is always better than dishonest attempt.
